proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(L^{0,(a)}=I_p-B^{0,(a)}\). By
\(\texttt{ass:shared-topological-order}\), simultaneous permutation by
\(\pi_0\) makes \(L^{0,(a)}\) unit lower triangular, so it is invertible.
Membership in \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\), through
\(\texttt{ass:centered-gaussian-law}\), says that the coordinates of
\(\varepsilon^{(a)}\) are independent and centered; the explicit
nondegeneracy clause in \(\texttt{def:published-limvam-class}\) says their
variances \(d_{ja}\) are strictly positive. Hence
\[
 \Omega^{aa}:=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\varepsilon^{(a)})
 =\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(d_{ja})\succ0.
\]
Using \(\texttt{ass:linear-structural-equations}\),
\[
 \Sigma^{aa}=(L^{0,(a)})^{-1}\Omega^{aa}(L^{0,(a)})^{-\mathsf T}\succ0.
 \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, for nonzero \(v\), the quadratic form in (1) equals the strictly
positive quadratic form of \(\Omega^{aa}\) at
\((L^{0,(a)})^{-\mathsf T}v\ne0\). Every principal matrix
\(\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\) is therefore positive definite and invertible.

By \(\texttt{def:modified-cholesky}\), if the predecessor set of \(r\) is
\(A\), the possibly nonzero part \(c\) of row \(r\) is characterized by the
normal equations
\[
 c\,\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]=\Sigma^{aa}[r,A].
\]
The inverse justified above gives the unique solution
\[
 c=\Sigma^{aa}[r,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1}.
\]
By \(\texttt{def:immutable-original-row}\), this is precisely
\(\beta^{(a)}(A,r)[A]\), and both definitions put zero in every column in
\(V\setminus A\). Thus
\[
 B_\pi^{(a)}[r,\cdot]=\beta^{(a)}(A,r).
\]
Reordering the coordinates of \(A\) permutes the normal equations and their
solution compatibly before the coordinates are restored to their original
labels. Suffix variables neither occur in these equations nor occupy a
nonzero column. This proves both invariance assertions.

Put \(L^{0,(a)}=I_p-B^{0,(a)}\) and
\(\mathcal L^0=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L^{0,(a)})\). By
\(\texttt{ass:shared-topological-order}\), every \(L^{0,(a)}\), and hence
\(\mathcal L^0\), is invertible. Component alignment gives, for the stacked
disturbance covariance \(\Omega\),
\[
 \Omega[(a,i),(b,j)]={\bf1}\{i=j\}\Gamma_i[a,b].
\]
After grouping indices by \(i\), this is
\(\operatorname{diag}_{i\in V}(\Gamma_i)\succ0\) by
\(\texttt{ass:disturbance-positive-definiteness}\). The structural
equations yield
\[
 \Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}
 = (\mathcal L^0)^{-1}\Omega(\mathcal L^0)^{-\mathsf T}\succ0.
 \tag{12}
\]
Consequently every \(\Sigma^{aa}\), every principal matrix
\(\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\), and every within-view Schur complement \(C_A^{aa}\)
is positive definite. All displayed inverses are therefore defined and
\(C_A^{aa}[r,r]>0\) for \(r\in U_A\).

Projection first onto the span of \(X_A^{(b)}\) and then onto the residual
of \(X_r^{(b)}\) equals projection onto the span of
\(X_{A\cup\{r\}}^{(b)}\), because the positive-definite Gram matrices make
each orthogonal projection unique. Hence, for
\(t\in U_A\setminus\{r\}\),
\[
 Z_{A\cup\{r\},t}^{(b)}=Z_{A,t}^{(b)}-
 \frac{C_A^{bb}[t,r]}{C_A^{bb}[r,r]}Z_{A,r}^{(b)}.
\]
Taking covariance with \(Z_{A,r}^{(a)}\) and using
\(\texttt{def:q-root-score}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(Z_{A,r}^{(a)},Z_{A\cup\{r\},t}^{(b)})
 =q^{ab}(A,r,t).
 \tag{13}
\]
This identity also proves that the residual state after removing \(A\) is
the path-independent state in \(\texttt{def:projected-residual-state}\).

Fix a suffix order of \(W=U_A\setminus\{r\}\). Sequential within-view
regression of \(Z_{A\cup\{r\},W}^{(b)}\) supplies an invertible unit
triangular residualizer \(K^{(b)}\) such that
\(e_W^{(b)}=K^{(b)}Z_{A\cup\{r\},W}^{(b)}\) and
\(e_r^{(a)}=Z_{A,r}^{(a)}\). Applying (13) coordinatewise gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_r^{(a)},e_W^{(b)})
 =\bigl(q^{ab}(A,r,t):t\in W\bigr)(K^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{14}
\]
Because \(K^{(b)}\) is invertible, the left side vanishes exactly when all
scores in (14) vanish. Exchanging \(a\) and \(b\) gives the corresponding
tail-to-root column criterion. Induction over successive roots, with the
one-coordinate suffix as the vacuous base case, therefore proves
\[
 \pi\text{ is a source-to-sink path in }\mathcal D_G
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})=0
 \text{ for every }\{a,b\}\in E.
 \tag{15}
\]
The within-view normal equations separately imply that each
\(R_\pi^{aa}\) is diagonal.

It remains to discharge the positive-definite completion clause. For any
candidate \(\pi\), set
\[
 \mathcal L_\pi=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L_\pi^{(a)}),
 \qquad S_\pi=\mathcal L_\pi\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}
 \mathcal L_\pi^{\mathsf T}.
\]
By (12) and invertibility of \(\mathcal L_\pi\), \(S_\pi\succ0\). For
\(j\in V\), let \(H_{\pi,j}\) be its principal submatrix on indices
\(\{(a,j):a\in M\}\). A nonzero vector extended by zeros shows directly
that \(H_{\pi,j}\succ0\). On every observed block,
\[
 S_\pi^{ab}=L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}=R_\pi^{ab},
\]
so \(H_{\pi,j}\) agrees with every specified entry of \(Q_{\pi,j}\) and
is a positive-definite completion. Combining this fact, (15), and
\(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\) proves the asserted equivalence with
\(\Pi_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\).

For a path satisfying (15), choose for each \(j\) an independent centered
Gaussian vector \((\eta_j^{(a)})_{a\in M}\) with covariance
\(H_{\pi,j}\), using an orthogonal diagonalization as in the proof of
\(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\). The stacks
are independent across \(j\), so their cross-coordinate covariances vanish;
each \(H_{\pi,j}\) is positive definite. Set
\(\eta^{(a)}=(\eta_j^{(a)}:j\in V)\) and
\(\widetilde X^{(a)}=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}\eta^{(a)}\). The coefficient
matrices share order \(\pi\), and diagonality from (15) implies that the
assembled disturbance covariance agrees with every \(R_\pi^{ab}\) on
observed blocks. Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X^{(a)},\widetilde X^{(b)})
 =(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}R_\pi^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{-\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma^{ab}
\]
for every diagonal or observed edge block. This is the required
component-aligned Gaussian completion with coefficient tuple \(T_\pi\).

Every ordering of \(V\setminus A\) is a legal suffix in the full removed-set
lattice, so suffix legality depends only on \(A\). Write such a suffix as
\((r_1,\ldots,r_{p-|A|})\) and set \(A_0=A\) and
\(A_s=A_{s-1}\cup\{r_s\}\). By
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), this suffix contributes, in
immutable original row labels,
\[
 \beta(A_0,r_1),\ \beta(A_1,r_2),\ \ldots,\
 \beta(A_{p-|A|-1},r_{p-|A|}).
 \tag{16}
\]
Every row in (16) depends only on the fixed observed marginals and the
displayed predecessor set. Thus the same suffix appends the same rows to
\(F(\rho)\) and \(F(\rho')\), proving
\[
 F(\rho)=F(\rho')\Longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Comp}(\rho)=\operatorname{Comp}(\rho').
 \tag{17}
\]

Conversely, all completion sets are nonempty because every full-lattice
prefix has a suffix. If one tuple \(T\) belongs to both completion sets,
no assigned row is overwritten, and
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\) shows that the projection of
\(T\) onto original rows indexed by \(A\) is both \(F(\rho)\) and
\(F(\rho')\). Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\cap\operatorname{Comp}(\rho')\ne\varnothing
 \Longrightarrow F(\rho)=F(\rho').
 \tag{18}
\]
Equality of nonempty completion sets implies an intersection, so (18) gives
the reverse implication in (17); its contrapositive gives the asserted
disjointness.

Let \(\mathcal P_A\) be the set of full-lattice prefixes from
\(\varnothing\) to \(A\). Induction on \(|A|\), using the insertion rule
in \(\texttt{def:fragment-hashcons-enumerator}\), gives
\[
 H_A=\{F(\rho):\rho\in\mathcal P_A\}.
 \tag{19}
\]
The initialization proves (19) for \(A=\varnothing\). For the induction
step, every prefix to \(A'\) has a last transition
\(A'\setminus\{r\}\to A'\); its parent fragment is present by induction,
and the algorithm writes exactly \(\beta(A'\setminus\{r\},r)\). Conversely,
every insertion extends a represented prefix by one full-lattice edge.
Exact trie equality removes only equal fragments, proving (19).

Fix \(F\in H_A\) and a representing prefix \(\rho\). Choose any suffix to
\(V\). By
\(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\), the resulting
permutation is in \(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\), and hence its tuple lies in
\(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\). By
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), every
\(T\in\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\) satisfies
\[
 T\big|_{\text{rows indexed by }A}=F.
 \tag{20}
\]
The completion sets attached to unequal fragments are nonempty and disjoint
by \(\texttt{lem:live-fragment-right-congruence}\). They are subsets of
\(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\), so
\[
 |H_A|\le|\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)|=N_{\mathrm{out}}.
 \tag{21}
\]
Summing (21) over the \(2^p\) subsets gives
\(\sum_A|H_A|\le2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\). Since a subset has at most \(p\)
outgoing transitions and each retained fragment is processed once, the
number of attempted transitions is at most
\[
 \sum_{A\subseteq V}(p-|A|)|H_A|
 \le p\sum_{A\subseteq V}|H_A|
 \le p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}.
\]

For every \(A\subseteq V\), induction on \(|A|\) exactly as in (19) gives
\[
 H_A=\{F(\rho):\rho\text{ is a full-lattice prefix ending at }A\}.
 \tag{22}
\]
Merging equal fragments is complete and preserves every continuation by
\(\texttt{lem:live-fragment-right-congruence}\). At \(A=V\), no row is
unassigned. By \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), the decoded sink
fragment of a permutation \(\pi\) is exactly \(T_\pi\). By
\(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\), all and only
the permutations in the full lattice belong to
\(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\), and the independently defined coefficient fiber
has no additional coefficient families. Therefore
\[
 \{\text{decoded members of }H_V\}
 =\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}
 =\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G).
 \tag{23}
\]
For a fixed original row label, lexicographic sorting compares all
exact-real coordinates and gives equal rows the same integer identifier.
Trie insertion creates a terminal only for the first occurrence of an
integer vector. Equation (23) is consequently emitted without omission and
with every numerical tuple emitted once.

We now count operations in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ER}}\). The full removed-set
lattice has \(2^p\) vertices and \(p2^{p-1}\) edges. Every vertex lies on
a source-to-sink path, so forward and backward pruning retain all vertices
and cost \(O(p2^p)\). For fixed \(A\) and view \(a\), one dense
factorization of \(\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\), followed by solving all rows indexed
by \(V\setminus A\), computes every \(\beta^{(a)}(A,r)\) leaving \(A\) in
\(O(p^3)\) field operations. The inverse exists by
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\). Over all subsets and views this
costs
\[
 O(mp^3 2^p).
 \tag{24}
\]

For a fixed row label \(r\), exactly \(K_r=2^{p-1}\) lattice edges carry
that label. Comparing two viewwise rows lexicographically examines at most
\(mp\) exact-real entries. Comparison sorting and adjacent equality
interning therefore cost
\[
 O\!\left(mp\sum_{r\in V}K_r\log(K_r+1)\right)
 =O(mp^3 2^p),
 \tag{25}
\]
because \(\log_2(K_r+1)=O(p)\). This is deterministic and uses no
real-valued hash.

Each row identifier uses \(O(p)\) bits, and a fragment has \(p\) identifier
slots. Lookup or insertion in a deterministic binary trie therefore costs
\(O(p^2)\) bit or pointer operations. By
\(\texttt{lem:projection-output-bound}\), at most
\(p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\) transitions are attempted, so propagation costs
\[
 O(p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}).
 \tag{26}
\]
Decoding \(m\) matrices with \(p^2\) entries for each output costs
\(O(mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}})\). The ancestry computation from
\(\texttt{prop:common-union-support-ancestry}\) adds
\(O(N_{\mathrm{out}}(mp^2+p^3))\), which is absorbed by (26) and the
decoding term because \(p,m\ge2\). Adding (24)--(26) gives the explicit
time bound in the statement.

For space, the interned rows occupy \(O(mp^2 2^p)\) real cells. The tries
occupy \(O(p^2 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}})\) bits or pointers by
\(\sum_A|H_A|\le2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\), and retained decoded outputs occupy
\(O(mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}})\) cells; the ancestry accumulator uses only
\(O(p^2)\) additional bits. The full-lattice edge list costs
\(O(p2^p)\). Since the output set is nonempty by
\(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\), these time and
space bounds are
\[
 O\!\left(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p
 \max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\}\right).
\]
Every propagation loop ranges over a retained fragment and an outgoing
subset edge. None ranges over permutations, and no cross-view residual
entry is used to screen an order.

Assume \(B^{0,(a)}=0\) for every \(a\in M\). By
\(\texttt{ass:linear-structural-equations}\),
\(X^{(a)}=\varepsilon^{(a)}\). The within-view product condition in
\(\texttt{ass:centered-gaussian-law}\) and the positive-variance clause in
\(\texttt{def:published-limvam-class}\) give a positive diagonal matrix
\(\Sigma^{aa}\). Hence, for every \(A\subseteq V\) and \(r\notin A\),
\[
 \Sigma^{aa}[r,A]=0,
 \qquad \beta^{(a)}(A,r)=0.
 \tag{27}
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), every order induces the same
all-zero tuple. By
\(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\), every one of
the \(p!\) orders is compatible for every \(G\), and hence in particular
when \(E=\varnothing\). It follows that
\[
 \Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{0\},\qquad N_{\mathrm{out}}=1.
\]
Starting with the unique empty fragment, every transition in
\(\texttt{def:fragment-hashcons-enumerator}\) writes a zero row by (27).
At any fixed subset all incoming paths therefore produce the same integer
fragment, which exact trie insertion retains once. The full lattice has all
\(2^p\) subset buckets, so exactly one fragment is retained in each and
exactly \(2^p\) in total.

Write every rational input coordinate in lowest terms with positive
denominator. For one principal regression solve, multiply its coefficient
matrix and right-hand side by the product \(d\) of the denominators of the
at most \((p+1)^2\) entries in the augmented matrix. If every input
numerator and denominator has at most \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\) binary digits,
then
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(d)\le(p+1)^2L_{\mathrm{bits}},
 \qquad \operatorname{bits}(dx)=O(p^2L_{\mathrm{bits}})
 \tag{28}
\]
for every scaled entry \(dx\). Scaling the entire augmented system by the
same positive integer leaves its solution unchanged. By
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), every principal within-view
covariance matrix is positive definite. Its leading principal minors in
any fixed ordering of \(A\) are therefore positive, so the no-pivot
fraction-free recurrence has no zero pivot.

The cited \(\texttt{lem:bareiss-minor-growth}\) gives exact integer division
and represents every transformed coefficient as a signed bordered minor of
the scaled augmented matrix. If a \(k\times k\) integer matrix \(K\) has
entries of magnitude below \(2^h\), the Leibniz formula gives
\[
 |\det K|
 \le\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_k}
 \prod_{i=1}^k|K_{i,\sigma(i)}|
 <k!\,2^{kh}.
\]
Consequently, using (28) and \(k\le p+1\),
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(\det K)
 \le kh+\lceil\log_2(k!)\rceil+1
 =O\!\left(p^3L_{\mathrm{bits}}+p\log p\right).
 \tag{29}
\]
The adjugate identity for the nonsingular principal covariance matrix
expresses every regression coordinate as a bordered-minor numerator divided
by its determinant. Reducing by the greatest common divisor and choosing a
positive denominator gives a canonical determinant-ratio certificate of
the bit length in (29). Two rational coordinates are equal exactly when
their canonical numerator-denominator pairs are equal, and two interned
rows are equal exactly when all their coordinate certificates agree.

The ordered exact-real proof of
\(\texttt{thm:exact-once-output-sensitive-enumeration}\) performs a number
of field operations and comparisons polynomial in \(p\), \(m\), \(2^p\),
and \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\). By (28)--(29), rational addition,
multiplication, division, sign comparison, and equality comparison act on
operands of polynomial binary length. Grade-school integer arithmetic is
polynomial in operand length. Euclid's algorithm is also polynomial: after
at most two remainder steps its positive second operand is less than half
its earlier value, so \(h\)-bit inputs require at most \(2h+1\) remainder
steps, each on operands of at most \(h\) bits. Fragment keys contain \(p\)
integer identifiers of \(O(p)\) bits and introduce no rational-expression
growth. Exact support tests for common ancestry compare canonical
numerators with zero and therefore have the same polynomial cost.

Multiplying these polynomial per-operation costs by the operation counts of
the exact-real theorem, then adding the total emitted encoding length,
proves the asserted polynomial bit time. Multiplying the height bound (29)
by the stored row and output counts, and adding the integer tries and the
\(p\times p\) Boolean ancestry accumulator, proves polynomial bit storage.
Every row is computed directly from an original principal covariance system,
so its height bound is not recursively iterated through the \(2^p\) subset
states. This proves that no superpolynomial intermediate or certificate
growth is forced in the stated rational regime.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\), and let \(\mathcal O_G\) be its observed moments for an arbitrary view graph \(G\). For every \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\), the fiber \(\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\) contains a centered jointly Gaussian mechanism whose common order is \(\pi\) and whose coefficient family is \(B_\pi\). Conversely, if \((\widetilde P,\widetilde B,\widetilde\varepsilon,\widetilde\pi)\in\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\) and \(\widetilde\pi=\pi\), then \(\widetilde B=B_\pi\). Consequently,
\[
 \Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)=\mathfrak S_V,
 \qquad
 \Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}.
\]
In the Gaussian witnesses, within-view disturbance coordinates are independent and nondegenerate, while off-diagonal cross-view residual covariances are retained as unrestricted nuisance covariances rather than tested for zero.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Stack the views in a fixed order, write
\(\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{Cov}_P((X^{(a)})_{a\in M})\), and
fix \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\). The argument in
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), applied within every view, shows
that \(\Sigma^{aa}\succ0\); hence all regressions defining
\(B_\pi^{(a)}\) exist. Put
\[
 \mathcal L_\pi=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L_\pi^{(a)}),
 \qquad
 S_\pi=\mathcal L_\pi\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}\mathcal L_\pi^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Each \(L_\pi^{(a)}\) is unit lower triangular after reindexing by \(\pi\),
so it is invertible. Since \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}\) is a covariance
matrix, (2) gives \(S_\pi\succeq0\).

We next identify its within-view blocks. Let
\(e_k^{(a)}\) be the residual from regressing
\(X_{\pi(k)}^{(a)}\) on
\((X_{\pi(1)}^{(a)},\ldots,X_{\pi(k-1)}^{(a)})\). The normal equations
give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_k^{(a)},X_{\pi(\ell)}^{(a)})=0
 \quad(\ell<k).
 \tag{3}
\]
For \(\ell<k\), the earlier residual \(e_\ell^{(a)}\) is a linear
combination of \(X_{\pi(1)}^{(a)},\ldots,X_{\pi(\ell)}^{(a)}\), all of
which lie in the predecessor span in (3). Therefore
\(\operatorname{Cov}_P(e_k^{(a)},e_\ell^{(a)})=0\). Moreover, positive
definiteness of \(\Sigma^{aa}\) implies that the residual variance is the
strictly positive Schur complement
\[
 d_{k,a}=\Sigma^{aa}[\pi(k),\pi(k)]-
 \Sigma^{aa}[\pi(k),A_{k-1}]
 \{\Sigma^{aa}[A_{k-1},A_{k-1}]\}^{-1}
 \Sigma^{aa}[A_{k-1},\pi(k)]>0.
 \tag{4}
\]
Thus every diagonal block \(S_\pi^{aa}=R_\pi^{aa}\) is diagonal with a
strictly positive diagonal.

Choose an orthogonal diagonalization
\(S_\pi=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{mp})U^{\mathsf T}\),
where \(\lambda_s\ge0\), and set
\(S_\pi^{1/2}=U\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\lambda_1},\ldots,
\sqrt{\lambda_{mp}})U^{\mathsf T}\). If \(g\) has \(mp\) independent
standard normal coordinates, define
\[
 \widetilde\varepsilon=S_\pi^{1/2}g,
 \qquad
 \widetilde X=\mathcal L_\pi^{-1}\widetilde\varepsilon.
 \tag{5}
\]
Then \(\widetilde\varepsilon\) is centered jointly Gaussian with covariance
\(S_\pi\), and
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X)
 =\mathcal L_\pi^{-1}S_\pi\mathcal L_\pi^{-\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}.
 \tag{6}
\]
For a fixed view \(a\), its disturbance covariance is the positive diagonal
matrix in (3)--(4). Its characteristic function therefore factors as
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\!\left(i\sum_{j\in V}t_j
 \widetilde\varepsilon_j^{(a)}\right)
 =\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12\sum_{j\in V}d_{j,a}t_j^2\right)
 =\prod_{j\in V}\exp(-d_{j,a}t_j^2/2),
\]
which proves that the within-view coordinates are independent, centered,
and nondegenerate. Equation (5) also gives
\(\widetilde X^{(a)}=B_\pi^{(a)}\widetilde X^{(a)}+
\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)}\), and the coefficient matrices share the order
\(\pi\). Thus the witness belongs to
\(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\). By (6), it matches every observed
diagonal block and edge block, so it belongs to
\(\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\). This proves existence in the first
direction. Notice that the cross-view blocks of \(S_\pi\) in (2), including
their off-diagonal coordinate entries, were carried into the Gaussian
witness without any zero constraint; they are nuisance covariance.

For the converse, take
\((\widetilde P,\widetilde B,\widetilde\varepsilon,
\widetilde\pi)\in\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\) with
\(\widetilde\pi=\pi\). Fix a view \(a\), a position \(k\), set
\(r=\pi(k)\), and let \(A=\{\pi(1),\ldots,\pi(k-1)\}\). The shared-order
condition makes row \(r\) of \(\widetilde B^{(a)}\) zero outside \(A\), so
the structural equation is
\[
 \widetilde X_r^{(a)}=
 \widetilde B^{(a)}[r,A]\widetilde X_A^{(a)}+
 \widetilde\varepsilon_r^{(a)}. \tag{7}
\]
The leading subsystem is triangular and therefore
\[
 \widetilde X_A^{(a)}=
 (I-\widetilde B^{(a)}[A,A])^{-1}widetilde\varepsilon_A^{(a)}.
 \tag{8}
\]
The product disturbance law within view \(a\) makes
\(\widetilde\varepsilon_r^{(a)}\) independent of
\(\widetilde\varepsilon_A^{(a)}\). By (8), it is therefore independent of
\(\widetilde X_A^{(a)}\); centeredness and finite second moments give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_{\widetilde P}
 (\widetilde\varepsilon_r^{(a)},\widetilde X_A^{(a)})=0.
 \tag{9}
\]
Taking covariance of (7) with \(\widetilde X_A^{(a)}\), using (9), and then
using fiber membership to replace the marginal covariance by the observed
one yields
\[
 \Sigma^{aa}[r,A]
 =\widetilde B^{(a)}[r,A]\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]. \tag{10}
\]
The matrix on the right is invertible by the marginal positive-definiteness
proved at the start of this argument, so
\[
 \widetilde B^{(a)}[r,A]
 =\Sigma^{aa}[r,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1}
 =B_\pi^{(a)}[r,A]. \tag{11}
\]
Both coefficient rows vanish outside \(A\). Since \(a\) and \(k\) were
arbitrary, \(\widetilde B=B_\pi\). Thus every coefficient in the fiber is
one of the \(T_\pi\), while the first direction realizes every such tuple.
Taking respectively the order and coefficient projections in
\(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\) and
\(\texttt{def:identified-tuple-set}\) proves
\[
 \Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)=\mathfrak S_V,
 \qquad
 \Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}.
\]

added_lemmas.statement: On an input generated by \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\), the relation \(\mathcal A_G(\mathcal O_G)\) is exactly the set of ordered pairs \((i,j)\) for which \(i\) is an ancestor of \(j\) in the union-support DAG of every tuple in \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\). Given the exact-once tuple stream, it is computable by exact zero tests, transitive closure, and intersection in \(O(N_{\mathrm{out}}(mp^2+p^3))\) additional time and \(O(p^2)\) working space beyond the tuple being processed.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\), the output
set is nonempty. For \(T\in\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\), choose
\(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\) with \(T=T_\pi\). The construction in
\(\texttt{def:modified-cholesky}\) places a nonzero entry
\(B_\pi^{(a)}[j,i]\) only when \(i\) precedes \(j\) in \(\pi\). Every
edge of \(\mathcal U(T)\) therefore points forward in \(\pi\), so

prose_updates.tldr: Under the published shared-order LiMVAM primitives, within-view product disturbances identify a modified-Cholesky coefficient tuple for each order, but unrestricted cross-view disturbance dependence makes every order covariance-compatible: off-diagonal cross-view residual entries are nuisance rather than valid root tests. The headline algorithm therefore traverses the full \(2^p\) removed-set lattice, interns immutable original-label regression rows, merges equal fragments, and emits every distinct published-class tuple exactly once. A separate component-aligned refinement retains the arbitrary-view-graph \(q\)-path and positive-definite coordinate-completion theorem. The full-lattice enumeration and common union-support ancestry computation require \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\})\) ordered exact-real time and space, with an output-polynomial rational bit implementation.

project_justification.gap: The parent calibration frontier had a \(2^p\)-state recursion but no noncircular method for enumerating distinct numerical coefficient tuples without following factorially many orders. It also risked treating component-aligned cross-view residual zeros as if they followed from the anchor's unrestricted cross-view model.
project_justification.niche: The covariance boundary separates two layers exactly. In the published unrestricted-cross-view layer, a transformed-full-covariance Gaussian witness realizes every order and within-view normal equations exhaust the independently defined mechanism fiber, so the exact compatibility graph is the full subset lattice. In the component-aligned subclass, the observable \(q\)-DAG remains an exact refinement. In both cases a row assigned at predecessor set \(A\) is the immutable original-label regression \(\beta(A,r)\).
project_justification.fill: Deterministic exact row interning and integer tries implement the full-lattice fragment quotient without a real hash oracle. Right congruence and projection charging bound every subset bucket by the number of distinct final tuples, and the output pass also intersects strict transitive closures of union-support graphs to return common ancestry.

sampling_model.design: The population input is the exact collection of view-marginal covariances and the cross-covariance blocks observed on an arbitrary fixed view graph \(G\). The published-class headline result uses the marginals to enumerate all orderwise coefficient tuples; observed cross-view off-diagonal residual covariances remain unrestricted nuisance. The component-aligned refinement may additionally use paired edge blocks through the \(q\)-tests.
sampling_model.units: Within each covariance source, observations are independent and identically distributed from the corresponding marginal of one target law \(P\). Different sources need not be independent because units may be reused.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment variable. The causal target is the coefficient projection of the published mechanism fiber, together with ancestry common to the union-support DAGs of all projected tuples.
sampling_model.overlap: Only edges of \(G\) require paired measurements. The published layer assumes centered finite-second-moment disturbances with independent, nondegenerate coordinates within each view and a shared order, while allowing arbitrary cross-view disturbance covariance. Component alignment and positive-definite coordinate-stack covariance are imposed only for the \(q\)-path refinement.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The new results are population-computational. Sampling uncertainty is handled only by the parent's covariance-region inversion over empirical marginal and edge covariance blocks; no new rate, limit law, or finite enumeration of a continuum-valued region inverse is claimed.

prose_updates.interpretation: Cross-view pairing does not reduce the coefficient frontier under unrestricted cross-view disturbance dependence, because any order's transformed residual covariance can itself serve as nuisance covariance for a Gaussian witness. The converse normal-equation argument shows that these modified-Cholesky tuples exhaust all mechanisms in the compatibility fiber. Pairing becomes order-informative only after an additional restriction such as component alignment. Computationally, the full published frontier can still be much smaller than the \(p!\) order set because many orders share the same immutable collection of regression rows.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The headline bound is total output-sensitive cost over an explicit \(2^p\) lattice, not polynomial delay and not polynomial time in \(p\). Ordered exact-real arithmetic does not imply floating-point stability; the separate rational theorem gives only a Turing-model bit bound. The component-aligned \(q\)-DAG is valid on its maintained subclass and does not extend to unrestricted cross-view dependence or arbitrary off-model nonchordal covariance arrays. The result enumerates an exact population tuple set, not a continuum-valued covariance-region inverse. Row sorting, integer tries, and transitive closure are non-novel implementation machinery.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The headline theorem concerns exact population enumeration under the published shared-order, within-view product-disturbance primitives with strictly positive within-view disturbance variances and arbitrary cross-view covariance. Its substantive boundary is negative for cross-view order screening but positive computationally: every order is covariance-compatible, every matching mechanism's coefficients are forced by within-view normal equations, and all distinct marginal modified-Cholesky tuples and their common union-support ancestry are emitted without order traversal. The stronger \(q\)-path certificate remains confined to the component-aligned subclass with positive-definite coordinate covariance blocks. No unrestricted causal uniqueness, polynomial-delay guarantee, off-model nonchordal preprocessing theorem, floating-point stability result, or continuum-region enumeration is claimed. The parent covariance-region inversion remains only the sampling-uncertainty layer.
